what_i_could_not_do: **THE PICTURES DID NOT LAND, AND THIS IS THE FIRST THING A CRITIC SHOULD ATTACK.** `CLAUDE.md`'s character directive is explicit that stills are not enough and that builders must look at the actual game in motion from multiple angles. I made FOUR attempts at a crowd frame and every one of them is recorded inside the tool rather than quietly retried: (1) a camera posed at the crowd centroid in SCENE coordinates returned an empty horizon, because `__HARNESS.camera({pos})` takes the SIMULATION's frame and at the Lilmoth stand the player is at world (2785.6, 5047) while the same people are DRAWN at (~0, ~0); (2) an offset taken from the gameplay camera's `look` was wrong by the camera's own look-ahead; (3) a 3.2 m portrait standoff on four named NPCs put the camera inside a wall on 4 of 4 — Lilmoth is a dense stilt town with no 3 m clear sightline to most of its people; (4) `listNPCs()` returns positions in the SAME frame as the drawn meshes, so the difference over all 60 matched pairs is (0, 35.387, 0) — which LOOKS like proof the frames coincide and is not, and a teleport computed from it put the player in open sea (photographed, then deleted with its run). What survives are **two real frames of Lilmoth from 22 m at 11 m of eye height** (`live/crowd-b000.png`, `crowd-b180.png`) whose camera rows are in `live/crowd-stance-live.json`, and **they contain no legible people**: b000 is a rooftop, b180 is a wall and a jetty. **So every claim in this file is a number and none of it is a look.** THE SCENE/SIM FRAME MISMATCH IS A CANDIDATE DEFECT IN ITS OWN RIGHT and it is not F10's — a capture tool cannot point a camera at a named NPC in a settlement cell, which is why five rounds of this item have photographed the player and never the crowd. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a harness method that returns the drawn-scene position of an eid, or one that poses the camera in the drawn frame. Until then the visual half of C3 arm (b) is unphotographed and a critic is entitled to score it that way.

**A CONTROL CLONE COULD NOT PHOTOGRAPH THE BEFORE ARM EITHER**, for the same reason, so there is no before/after frame pair — only a before/after NUMBER pair. The clone itself is real and clean (`git archive c43ce8ca game tools` into a scratch tree, 56 MB, no `.git`, its OWN copy of the tool run from inside it per HAZARDS §22), and it reproduces the r10 critic's live numbers to the digit. It is the numbers that are paired, not the pixels.

**I DID NOT WIRE THE STANCE INTO `syncEntities` — THE ENEMY STATIC FALLBACK — AND MY PREDECESSOR DID.** `renderer.js:706` calls `poseStatic` for any entity whose `poseFromRig` returns false, and the quarantined work passed the stance there too. I left it alone deliberately: an entity on that path is either DEAD (the same line sets `mesh.scale.y = 0.18`) or not yet built, and dealing a corpse a seeded weight-shift stance is a claim I have not measured. REVERSIBLE, one argument: if a critic finds body-less enemies standing in the old shared A-pose in a frame, add `stance` to that call — the solver is population-agnostic and its planting arm covers any actor.

**RI-VIS10's OTHER SEVENTEEN CHECKS DID NOT MOVE AND I SCORED NONE OF THEM.** I measured C3 arm (b) and nothing else. B1, C4 and D4 still need a fresh judge no builder or critic can spawn (`CLAUDE.md` rule 0e — **the orchestrator has owed these for three verdicts**); D1's garment vocabulary still does not exist; D2 and D5 remain the cheapest unrun censuses in the item and have been for three rounds; E1 is still 14 drawn bodies for 408 records. A critic re-running `f10-r9c-crowd-census.mjs` and the C2 mask machinery would be measuring the most likely place my work shows up in the score.

**JOB 3 — THE PUPIL AT DISTANCE — IS RULED TO BE A LATER ROUND'S WORK, AND HERE IS THE RULING.** The r10 critic verified the pupil reads at 0.475 m and is two amber smudges at 2.486 m, with *'no lid, no orbit'* still standing. one_number_that_moved_the_wrong_way_and_.the_red_arm: L2 STABILITY failed on its first two runs, reporting 31 of 60 people 'shuffling'. **The instrument was talking, not the build**: `worst_C3_shift_deg` read 0.000000 in the same report, which is the tell. The signature rounds `inverse(group) * bone` to 4 dp and that recomposition carries ~1e-12 m of float round-off, so a value on a rounding boundary flips the hash without anything moving. I replaced the criterion with the PHYSICAL quantity — no non-foot bone drifts more than 1 micron — measured per bone rather than hashed, and **left both hash counts published beside it**, because deleting the number that looked bad is the move this project's doctrine exists to stop. The per-bone table is in the artifact: `foot_l` 22.39 mm and `foot_r` 10.51 mm (the terrain conform, tracking the ground under a walking person, and pre-existing since round 7), every other bone <= 2.842e-12 m.
